title: Minimax Estimation of Average Conditional Hellinger Distance over Growing Alphabets
banked_reason: Math referee pass; kernel_substituted@oeq:joint-frontier and kernel_substituted@oeq:propensity-price remain unrepaired; general referee incremental, paper_score_ceiling 4.5 < 7.4, meets_floor=false; independent validity gate confirms below field floor.
gap_reasons: The promised sharp closed-form joint frontier, attaining observable estimator, and necessary-and-sufficient consistency boundary are not delivered: this node remains an open question with only an unmatched baseline/converse bracket, so the current artifact has no headline Stat theorem or usable frontier.

The promised supplied-propensity rate and algebraic characterization of an unbounded information price remain open; the displayed unmatched ratio ceiling is diagnostic rather than the requested deliverable.

The delivered results establish a baseline upper bound and specialized equality, zero-face, and sparse-row converses; the full-class matched result covers only d=1,k=2. In the dense regime, the baseline dk/n and zero-face lower bound D/[n log(eD)] leave a logarithmic gap, while at D of order n the bounds do not even settle uniform consistency. The factorial certificate and fixed-sample transfer supply implementation machinery, but no polynomial rule receives the dimension-uniform certificate needed to resolve joint-frontier, and propensity-price also remains open. The framing explicitly identifies these questions as open and contains no stale assertion of a completed sharp frontier, but the advertised estimation and resolution guidance remains undelivered. The checked [Han–Jiao–Weissman Theorem 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1605.09124v2) concerns aggregate squared Hellinger under direct sampling; the internal technique-donor writeups have no supplied public theorem text and contribute no independently checked comparator theorem. The 4.5 score reflects the narrow converse contribution, unresolved attainable precision and consistency boundary, and application evidence limited to target diagnostics in an experiment differing from the metro design. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 4.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Derived a total original-record baseline estimator, specialized equality and sparse-row converses, a normalized zero-face moment-matching converse, and exact factorial-energy/fixed-record transfer machinery. The supporting math passed review, but no public pilot-local polynomial achieves dimension-uniform bias, full mixed-derivative energy, and pilot-variance bounds, leaving the dense logarithmic gap and intermediate-occupancy consistency boundary open. The promised sharp joint frontier and propensity-information price remain undelivered; the independent validity gate confirmed banking at incremental under the field floor, with no Lean formalization attempted.
tldr: Context-specific categorical distributions can change even when the intervention marginals coincide. The causal target \(C(P)\) averages unsquared Hellinger distances across contexts before marginalization. The research question is the sharp original-record mean-squared-error frontier jointly in \(n,d,k\), with an observable attaining estimator and a normalized converse over the entire overlap class. Equality, outcome zeros, and unpaired sparse contexts must be handled together. The numerical rate is an output of the research question. The intended contribution is a subfield advance in functional estimation; the applied use is prospective precision guidance for disruption flow profiles.
gap: Direct categorical squared-Hellinger estimation and scalar discrete-confounding estimation are settled in their respective settings, but the checked sources do not give this conditional unsquared scalar-functional frontier.
fill: The joint question requires an evaluated algebraic rate, a total original-record procedure, and a matching converse on \(\mathcal P(d,k)\). Supporting baseline and boundary results are retained as checks rather than substituted for that deliverable.
